industrial_candidate.basis: Lowest deterministic canonical catalyst/process-dependent cost among all optimized candidates in the full admissible process window.

highest_atomic_activity.reference_condition: T 673.0 K, pN2 24.5 bar, pH2 74.25 bar, pNH3 1.0 bar

parity_and_reachability.interpretation: Ru would need about 201x intrinsic activity improvement to match Fe cost, but the frozen descriptor manifold provides at most about 2.52x across process states; intrinsic-activity improvement alone cannot make Ru cost-competitive under this model.

vessel_floor.note: Ru and Os converter volumes are below the vessel-correlation floor and were costed with the declared clamp; Fe is not below the floor.

chosen_args.why_stop: Stopping rule satisfied: every candidate was optimized in the full admissible process window, Fe is the deterministic lowest-cost feasible candidate, no candidates remain unresolved, and the required Ru-vs-Fe intrinsic-activity parity/reachability assessment was completed with an unreachable classification. Remaining affordable actions such as lever sensitivity or exact dominance checks would not change the canonical deterministic industrial decision and have low expected decision value relative to established evidence.

unresolved_decision_risk.primary_risk: Descriptor uncertainty can make Ru lower-cost than Fe in a non-negligible fraction of MC draws among feasible candidates.
unresolved_decision_risk.interpretation: The industrial recommendation is Fe for the frozen nominal descriptor table and canonical cost model. Under declared descriptor uncertainty, Ru is the main residual challenger, but deterministic parity via intrinsic activity alone is unreachable on the frozen descriptor scaling manifold, and Os is not competitive in the MC sample.
model_boundary_risks: Fe optimum is at the Tsep upper edge, so a broader separation-temperature domain could alter the optimum outside the declared admissible domain.
Ru and Os optima are at the T upper edge and below the vessel-correlation floor, but this does not overturn Fe because Ru and Os are already more costly under the declared clamped cost model.
